messages:
mira: heads-up: after kernel-selector v2.3 rollout to canary we see a small-write surge causing host p99 to climb (50ms -> 92ms) and sys CPU up ~20%. spotted around 22:10 UTC.
deepak: grabbing traces. initial signal: massive increase in writev counts coming off tokenizer and proxy layers.
toni: kvcache dashboard shows write-back queue depth spiking and per-shard async-flush latency increasing. looks like many tiny fragments are forcing extra index ops.
mira: sanitized log snippet:
```
INGRESS: got req
tokenizer: emit 56b chunk
proxy: writev([hdr,56b,ctrl]) -> flush
kernel: syscall writev -> 3 syscalls total
```
mira: previously those would be buffered to ~800-1200b and one syscall. v2.3 seems to narrow the batching window for the chosen kernel.
evan: kernel-selector metric shows it favored "ultra-low-latency" kernels for the flow which reduced the allowed batch_ms from 8 -> 1. That explains the scatter of small writes.
deepak: flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/3142000001 shows syscall hotspots at tokenize->writev->epoll.
perf-bot: nightly-regression: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/9123/diff/3142000001 flagged p99 regression (+42ms).
toni: short-term mitigation: enable proxy flag proxy.coalesce_small_frames=true which buffers up to 10ms per stream and coalesces by request id. microbench locally shows writev count -68%, p99 down to ~54ms.
mira: plan: flip on 20% canary at 3142000040, watch ingress_p99, sys_cpu, kvcache_async_flush_qdepth for 15m. rollback if p99 > 80ms or errors > 0.4%.
evan: long-term: we should expose a "write_tolerance" hint in kernel-selector; kernels can opt-in that they tolerate larger batching windows. then selector can trade a few ms of decode time for much fewer syscalls and lower host overhead when write_density > X.
deepak: experiment notes: proxy.coalesce_small_frames=true -> writev calls -68%, kvcache-async-latency -35%, CPU sys% -12% in our lab burst test. added numbers to PR.
toni: i'll add an alert: kvcache.hot_shard_evictions > 6/sec during the canary window.
mira: rolling the runtime flip now. will post updates and perf snapshots to incidents after 10m. tagging @evan for kernel-selector follow up.
